phase3_findings.description: Under any dialect other than mysql, verify_base_tables forces the called-function list to empty, so a statement referencing no relation but calling a function returns success without a check or log line; the `checked = ... if dialect == "mysql" else "relation types"` branch only served SQLite and now has no reachable non-MySQL dialect. Config load refuses every non-MySQL URL, so production cannot reach this path.

report:
## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (one Suggestion-level checklist failure, one Suggestion-level reviewer finding, eight inconclusive checklist items)
The PR is ready to merge: no finding or checklist failure reaches the `important` threshold, and all 28 acceptance criteria are itemized in the checklist.
Rule applied: rule 6 — only findings below the threshold and inconclusive items remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (2)

<details><summary>2 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/safety/relations.py` lines 105 to 121: under any dialect other than `mysql`, the function-call check is skipped without a log line, and the `checked = ... if dialect == "mysql" else "relation types"` branch now has no reachable non-MySQL dialect. Config load refuses every non-MySQL URL, so production cannot reach this path. (raised by 1/5 agents)
- VC-52: FAIL (suggestion) — The first question creates ./examples/mysql-demo/chroma/ (persist_dir is resolved relative to the working directory, the repo root). [examples/mysql-demo/README.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  README (examples/mysql-demo/README.md:42-43) says the first question creates ./examples/mysql-demo/chroma/. The README's own command `sqllens serve -c examples/mysql-demo/sqllens.toml` runs run_preflight(cfg) before run(cfg) (src/sqllens/cli.py:241-249). The preflight includes probe_memory (src/sqllens/preflight.py:245), which calls persist_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) (preflight.py:185-188) and so creates the directory at server startup, before any question. The directory is also created by `validate --check-memory`. The ChromaAgentMemory construction does no I/O (tools/_agent.py:36 comment), so the directory is not created lazily by the first question unless --no-preflight is set. The relative-path part is correct: persist_dir = './examples/mysql-demo/chroma' (sqllens.toml:24) is passed unchanged as str(cfg.memory.persist_dir) (agent/factory.py:154-155), so it resolves against the working directory. Chroma's own files (chroma.sqlite3) are likely first written on the first question, but the directory itself is not.

  </details>

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred (8)

<details><summary>8 items</summary>

- VC-62: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — sqlglot's exp.Table.db returns the schema qualifier string (or empty) for MySQL-parsed tables such as mysql.user, and is_catalog_table relies on it alone. [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  No dependency_sources and sqlglot is not in the views, so Table.db could not be read. readonly.py:273 does rely solely on (table.db or '').lower(). Missing: sqlglot/expressions.py class Table.db.

  </details>

- VC-71: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — test_validate_mysql_stand_in_url_opens_no_connection patches socket.socket.connect/connect_ex; pymysql's connection path uses socket.create_connection, which calls socket.socket.connect, so a connect attempt would be recorded. [tests/unit/test_cli.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The test (tests/unit/test_cli.py:143-169) patches socket.socket.connect and connect_ex as claimed. The claim rests on pymysql's installed connections.py using socket.create_connection, but the item has no dependency_sources and pymysql is not vendored in the views; a search of the worktree .venv found no pymysql/connections.py. Directories searched: view-head and the worktree .venv. The library source was not read, so the claim cannot be settled.

  </details>

- VC-76: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — sqlglot.parse_one('SELECT * FROM table_info(\'t\')', dialect='mysql').find(exp.Table) returns a non-None exp.Table node (the test asserts table is not None) [tests/unit/test_safety.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The test at tests/unit/test_safety.py:1240-1241 parses "SELECT * FROM table_info('t')" with dialect='mysql', calls find(exp.Table) and asserts the result is not None. requirements.txt:104 pins sqlglot==30.31.0. This is a library claim, but the item has no dependency_sources and the sqlglot source is not in the head view. I did not read the sqlglot parser, so I cannot confirm that its MySQL parser wraps a function call in FROM as exp.Table(this=Anonymous). I did not run sqlglot.parse_one either. Not verified: sqlglot 30.31.0 source, parser _parse_table / _parse_table_parts.

  </details>

- VC-79: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — MySQL returns a quoted alias (with spaces/padding) as a column label exactly as written [tests/unit/test_safety_masking.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The claim is the comment at tests/unit/test_safety_masking.py:247-248 ("a quoted alias, which MySQL returns exactly as written"). The test at 246-252 only asserts matcher behavior and uses a trailing-space label ("token_count "). Whether MySQL returns a quoted alias exactly as written depends on MySQL server naming (Item::set_name), not on repository code. It is not in the views and no dependency_sources were supplied, so I could not read it. From memory, the server keeps trailing spaces in an explicit alias but strips leading non-graph characters, which would make the absolute wording "exactly as written" and "padding included" inaccurate for leading spaces. I did not run MySQL or PyMySQL to confirm.

  </details>

- VC-83: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — Outside MySQL (tsql, None) a SHOW statement parses to an exp.Command that assert_select_only rejects [tests/unit/test_safety.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  readonly.py:545-560 shows assert_select_only rejects any root that is not exp.Show or in _ALLOWED_ROOT_TYPES (exp.Command is not allowed), so the gate side holds. Whether sqlglot's tsql and default dialects parse SHOW TABLES to exp.Command is library behavior. No dependency_sources were supplied, and sqlglot source is not in the views (inventory.json has no sqlglot parser.py entry). The installed copies I found sit outside the views and were not read. Not settled: sqlglot parser/tokenizer COMMANDS handling of SHOW for tsql and default dialects, and no run of assert_select_only('SHOW TABLES', dialect='tsql'/None) was made.

  </details>

Run `sqllens validate --check-db -c examples/mysql-demo/sqllens.toml`. It exits 0. 3. Query the demo database as the demo config's user for the number of albums whose artist is `AC/DC`. It returns 2. Static findings only: examples/mysql-demo/sqllens.toml:16 has read_only = true; :24 persist_dir = ./examples/mysql-demo/chroma (under examples/mysql-demo/); :14 user chinook_reader. Chinook_MySql.sql:257 Artist 1 = AC/DC; Album inserts at :534 and :537 show AlbumId 1 and 4 with ArtistId 1 (the dump's remaining Album rows were not exhaustively counted). It names The Chinook Database (https://github.com/lerocha/chinook-database), release v1.4.5 and its URL https://github.com/lerocha/chinook-database/releases/tag/v1.4.5, and it carries 'Copyright (c) 2008-2024 Luis Rocha' plus an MIT permission notice. issue-context.md:124 (issue-side, not upstream) says the v1.4.5 LICENSE.md reads 'Copyright (c) 2008-2024 Luis Rocha', which matches. checklist.verify_hint: Check how persist_dir is resolved and whether the dir is created lazily on first query or at serve/validate
checklist.evidence: README (examples/mysql-demo/README.md:42-43) says the first question creates ./examples/mysql-demo/chroma/. The README's own command `sqllens serve -c examples/mysql-demo/sqllens.toml` runs run_preflight(cfg) before run(cfg) (src/sqllens/cli.py:241-249). The preflight includes probe_memory (src/sqllens/preflight.py:245), which calls persist_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) (preflight.py:185-188) and so creates the directory at server startup, before any question. The directory is also created by `validate --check-memory`. The ChromaAgentMemory construction does no I/O (tools/_agent.py:36 comment), so the directory is not created lazily by the first question unless --no-preflight is set. The relative-path part is correct: persist_dir = './examples/mysql-demo/chroma' (sqllens.toml:24) is passed unchanged as str(cfg.memory.persist_dir) (agent/factory.py:154-155), so it resolves against the working directory. Chroma's own files (chroma.sqlite3) are likely first written on the first question, but the directory itself is not.
